page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with 26 vCPUs and 234 GB of RAM. The compute resources are powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, offering 13 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core and a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The CPU features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). For acceleration, the server includes a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM, alongside a bundled 804 GB NVMe SSD for local storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2072.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 33.6 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14893.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 35694.46. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 2213.07 GB/sec, which drops to 159.18 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 348.05 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, but drops to an average of 23.8 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model, and a poor 2.49 tokens/sec for a large 70B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of specialized hardware, including the H100 GPU and AMX-enabled Intel Xeon processor, represents a significant resource commitment designed for specialized workloads rather than general-purpose computing. The primary tradeoff lies in the drop-off in LLM inference performance as model sizes scale up, indicating that while the single H100 GPU is highly efficient for smaller models, larger models exceed its optimal threshold. This server is suited for machine learning training and inference of small-to-medium models, data science pipelines, and accelerated database operations.
